sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A small species. Head and pronotum ochraceous orange, the latter usually tinged with brown; thorax and wing buds very dark to nearly blackish brown; abdominal tergites black; wings smoky, with darker veins. Head (Fig. 55) small, round, convex on top, with few hairs. Compound eyes small (0.18 × 0.23), not prominent. Ocelli small, distinctly separate from the compound eyes. Antennae 13—15-segmented. Pronotum large, wider than the head, wider than long, the anterior margin slightly concave, the sides rounded, the posterolateral angles oblique, the posterior margin distinctly wavy, sparsely covered with short fine hairs. Wings broad; the subcostal vein of the fore wing very short to more than twice the width of the wing at the suture; the radial vein more than twice the width at the suture, sometimes single, sometimes forked near the base or near the apex; radial sector with 9—12 branches, some forked; media parallel to the radial sector, distinctly nearer the radial sector than the cubitus; cubitus distinctly above the middle at the widest part of the wing. Tibial spurs serrate. Measurements (mm): length with wings 9.00—9.50; length without wings 4.50; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.32—1.46; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.95—1.07; head width 1.60—1.13 (thus in the original); pronotum length 0.66—0.77; pronotum width 1.21—1.24; fore wing length 7.00—7.25; fore wing width 2.49. Queen body length 13.38.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head ochraceous orange, darker in front but never heavily tinged with brown. Head (Fig. 56) long and narrow, less than half as wide as long, the sides nearly parallel, sometimes slightly narrowing in front, with few hairs. Frons slightly wrinkled, with a rather broad depression that runs from the anterior dorsal margin to the clypeus and widens in front, the suture usually very distinct. Compound eyes small, degenerate, oval, near the antennal fossae. Ocelli degenerate or absent. Antennae 12—14-segmented, usually 12, rarely 14. Mandibles with 3 teeth on the left and 2 on the right, all directed forwards, the teeth on the left evenly spaced, the basal tooth slightly smaller than the others. Pronotum usually slightly narrower than the head, the anterior margin slightly concave, the sides nearly parallel, the posterolateral angles rounded, the posterior margin slightly wavy. Tibial spurs serrate. Measurements (mm; three columns in the original: in parentheses the mean of the 6 offspring of one recently mated pair, then the range, then the mean): body length (5.00) / 5.25—6.50; head length including mandibles (2.12) / 2.56—3.06 / 2.83; head length (to clypeal suture) (1.57) / 1.83—2.20 / 2.08; head width (1.02) / 1.10—1.28 / 1.21; gula width at the narrowest point (0.18) / 0.16—0.22 / 0.19; pronotum length (0.44) / 0.55—0.77 / 0.69; pronotum width (0.84) / 0.95—1.24 / 1.15.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); it was named by Hill in 1925, under the old combination Calotermes (Calotermes) rufinotum. Measurements in mm. Distribution: Victoria, Seaford (type locality), Lakes Entrance, Cockatoo, Jamieson; New South Wales, Eden, Mt. Kosciusko, Captain's Flat and others. Taxonomic doubt: in 1921 Hill misidentified this species as C. obscurus (nec Walker). OCR doubt: in the alate the head width "1.60 - 1.13" has its values reversed and is probably "1.06 - 1.13"; the text records the original as printed and flags it. In the soldier measurement table the head column was OCRed as "Average of six /£gPiL e specimens" and is read, from the footnote "Progeny of a recently mated pair", as offspring specimens; "G-ula" is a misreading of "Gula".
